title: RunEvent
description: One event of a run, in the order the run produced it.

at.description:
Wall-clock time the event was produced, to the millisecond; on the
wire, milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

seq.description:
Zero-based position of the event in its run's stream; consecutive
events differ by one.

RunEventKind.description:
What a [`RunEvent`] reports.

[`Self::Completed`] is always the last event, including for a run that
failed or was cancelled, unless the run itself was dropped before it
finished; then the stream ends without it. New kinds may be added.

oneOf.description:
The run's turn was admitted to its session and is about to send its
first model request, or the compaction requests that precede it (see
[`Self::Compacted`]). A run that fails before admission, such as
one whose session is busy, emits only [`Self::Completed`].

model.description:
Catalog identifier of the model, when the harness selected it
from a [`crate::ModelCatalog`]; `None` for a model the host
supplied directly.

session.description:
Session the turn belongs to; a one-shot run reports its
in-memory session.

turn.description: Durable position of the run's turn within its session.

oneOf.description:
An item started. Its content arrives with [`Self::ItemCompleted`]
for the same `id`, unless the run fails or is cancelled first: an
item still open when [`Self::Completed`] arrives was interrupted
and never completes. So was a tool-call item a streamed model
response opened when that response was discarded, such as a response
that failed or an invalid final answer that was requested again; the
discarded response's reasoning and message items complete with the
text it streamed.

A fragment of an open item's content as the model streams it,
between the item's [`Self::ItemStarted`] and [`Self::ItemCompleted`].

Only the built-in [`crate::model::ModelClient`] streams, for
providers on the Responses and Chat Completions protocols, and only
for the run's turn requests. A response's reasoning streams into a
[`ItemKind::Reasoning`] item, its text into a [`ItemKind::Message`]
item, and each tool call's arguments into that call's
[`ItemKind::ToolCall`] item, each started at its first fragment.
Fragments of one item concatenate to its streamed content; the
completed item stays authoritative.

id.description: Identifier of the item, as [`Self::ItemStarted`] reported it.

oneOf.description: An item finished with its content.

id.description: Identifier of the item, as [`Self::ItemStarted`] reported it.

oneOf.description:
A tool call that changes state waits for the harness's
[`crate::approval::ApprovalHandler`], which the harness asks right
after this event. It falls between the call's [`Self::ItemStarted`]
and [`Self::ItemCompleted`]; a call the handler did not decide on in
time fails the run with [`ErrorKind::ApprovalTimeout`].

request.description: The call waiting for a decision.

oneOf.description:
A model request completed, with the tokens its provider reported.
The usage and cost of these events sum to the run outcome's
[`crate::RunOutcome::usage`] and [`crate::RunOutcome::cost`].
Later per-request fields may be added, so match it with `..`.

cost.description:
Price of `usage` at the prices of `model`, the model that
answered this request, or `None` when that model has no
[`crate::catalog::Pricing`].

model.description:
Catalog identifier of the model that answered this request, such
as the summary model answering a round summary request, when the
harness selected it from a [`crate::ModelCatalog`]; `None` for a
model the host supplied directly.

oneOf.description:
The next model request is sent reduced to fit the context budget.
Counts describe that whole request, so a reduction carried over from
an earlier request is reported again.

Under [`crate::model::ContextPolicy::AutoCompact`], the session tried
to compact earlier turns before the run's first turn request. It
follows [`Self::Started`] and the [`Self::ModelRequestCompleted`]
events of the compaction requests, each emitted as it completed. The
turn's [`crate::turn::HistoryActivity`] counts what its first request
still evicted.

A model request of the run, a turn request or a compaction or round
summary request, failed transiently and is retried after `after`, as
its provider's [`crate::provider::RetryPolicy`] allows. It is
emitted before the wait, so cancelling the run then stops it. A turn
request that still fails after its last retry fails the run; a
summary request's failure is handled as that summary's failure.

Only the built-in [`crate::model::ModelClient`] reports retries, and
only from the task that sends the request; a custom
[`crate::Model`] that retries on its own emits none. Later fields
may be added, so match it with `..`.

after.description:
Delay before the retry is sent, to the millisecond; on the wire,
whole milliseconds.

attempt.description: One-based number of this retry within its model request.

kind.description:
The failure being retried: [`ErrorKind::RateLimited`] for a
`429`, [`ErrorKind::Overloaded`] for a `5xx`, or
[`ErrorKind::Transport`] for a connection failure.

oneOf.description:
The run offers native-sandboxed `bash`, the sandbox cannot run on
this host, and the harness runs the run's commands without isolation
instead, as [`crate::sandbox::IfUnavailable::Unsandboxed`], the
default, allows. It is emitted once per such run, before its first
turn request, and names what is missing and how to fix it, as the
turn's [`crate::TurnReport::sandbox_warning`] does; the model-facing
`bash` description states that commands run without isolation. For
[`crate::sandbox::SandboxUnavailableReason::UnixSocketsUnsupported`]
the commands still run inside the sandbox, without the socket grants.

The run finished; always the last event. It follows the run's
settlement, so once it arrives the session transcript holds the
turn of a run that emitted [`Self::Started`] with its terminal
status, unless persistence cleanup failed (see
[`crate::RunOutcome::settlement`]). A run that stopped before
[`Self::Started`] may have recorded no turn.

ModelId.description:
Catalog key of one model, unique within a [`super::ModelCatalog`].

Built-in entries use `provider/model`, such as `openai/gpt-6-luna`, so a
model served by two providers, such as an `OpenAI` model reached with an
API key or through a `ChatGPT` plan, has two distinct identifiers.

SessionId.description: Identifier of the session a run's turn belongs to.

TurnIndex.description: Durable position of a turn within its session.

ItemId.description:
Identifier of one item within its run, assigned in the order items
start.

ItemKind.description: What an item is, known when it starts.

oneOf.description: Assistant text written beside tool calls, or streamed by a response.
The run's final output.
Provider reasoning the model returned.
A tool call and its result.

Delta.description:
A fragment of streamed item content, carried by
[`RunEventKind::ItemDelta`].

oneOf.description: Assistant text of a [`ItemKind::Message`] item.

Provider reasoning of a [`ItemKind::Reasoning`] item, such as a
reasoning summary.

Arguments of a [`ItemKind::ToolCall`] item's call, as JSON text that
is incomplete until the last fragment.

Assistant text the model wrote beside its tool calls, or the text a
streamed response wrote as it went (see [`RunEventKind::ItemDelta`]):
for a final answer, its raw text, which [`Self::Output`] then carries
validated. A final answer that did not stream emits only
[`Self::Output`].

The validated final output of a successful run, emitted after the
turn committed and directly before [`RunEventKind::Completed`]; a
failed or cancelled run has none.

Provider reasoning returned with a model response: its plain text,
or the summary of encrypted or signed reasoning. Reasoning without
readable text, such as encrypted reasoning with an empty summary,
emits no item.
A tool call and its result.

RunOutput.description:
Validated final output of a successful run.

It serializes as `{"type": "json" | "text", "value": ...}`.

oneOf.description: JSON output validated against the run's output schema.
The final assistant text of a run in text output mode.

ToolCallStatus.description: How a tool call was answered.

oneOf.description:
The tool ran; a `bash` result reports the command's own exit status,
and a host tool's oversized output is dropped.

The tool rejected the call, such as malformed arguments or a path
outside the repository, and the model was told why.

The call was answered without running: a repeat of an earlier read,
or a read deferred to a later response.
The tool is denied by policy or does not exist.

The [`crate::approval::ApprovalHandler`] denied the call, which did
not run; the model received the denial's feedback.

The call was answered, as a [`crate::TurnRecord`] reports every
answered call: sessions store the result text but not which of the
statuses above the live run reported.

The turn stopped before the call was answered, as a
[`crate::TurnRecord`] reports it; the output is empty.

ToolCallItem.description: A tool call the model made and the result it was answered with.

arguments.description:
Arguments as the model sent them, as JSON text; arguments the tool
could not decode are kept verbatim and may not be valid JSON.

likely_sandbox_denial.description:
Whether a `bash` call ran inside the sandbox and failed with an
operating-system denial the sandbox may have caused, as
[`ToolActivity::BashLikelySandboxDenial`] reports; the result told
the model. It is advisory, and the command's own output can set it:
never rerun a command outside the sandbox automatically; route any
such rerun through the user's approval with the exact command.
`false` in a [`crate::TurnRecord`], since sessions do not store it.

output.description:
Result text the model received; empty for a call that was never
answered.

summary.description:
Bounded one-line description of what the call did; empty in a
[`crate::TurnRecord`], since sessions do not store it.

ApprovalRequest.description: One tool call waiting for its [`Decision`].

arguments.description: Arguments the model sent, as a JSON object.

command.description:
For a call marked [`ToolEffects::ExecutesUnsandboxed`], the exact
argument vector, executable first, it runs with outside the sandbox
if [`Decision::AllowUnsandboxed`] approves it, with no shell between;
`None` for every other call.

effects.description:
What the call may change, as its tool declares it for these
arguments; allowing [`ToolEffects::ExecutesUnsandboxed`] lets the
command run outside the sandbox with the host's full access.

run.description:
Run that made the call; `None` for a call outside a run, such as one
from [`crate::Harness::turn`].

session.description:
Host-created session whose turn made the call; `None` for a
stateless run or turn.

tool.description: Function name of the called tool.

ToolEffects.description:
What one tool call may change.

With a [`crate::approval::ApprovalHandler`] configured, every call to a
tool that is not [`Self::ReadOnly`] waits for its decision.

oneOf.description: Reads state without changing it, like the built-in `read`.

Changes state outside the model's context, such as workspace files
or records in another system, like the built-in `write`.

Runs commands or other actions whose effects the harness cannot
bound, like the built-in `bash`.

Runs a command outside the sandbox with the harness process's full
access, like a `bash` call of a program
`BashConfig::with_excluded_command` excludes. It runs unsandboxed
only when the approval handler decides
[`crate::approval::Decision::AllowUnsandboxed`]; a plain allow runs
it inside the sandbox. Show the user the exact argument vector, since
the program can run any code its arguments name.

RunId.description:
Identifier of one run, unique across processes.

Every [`crate::Run`] has one: each event of its stream carries it, and
each of its tool calls sees it in [`crate::tool::ToolContext::run_id`].

Cost.description:
Price of some [`Usage`] in integer micro-USD, one millionth of a US
dollar, with where its prices came from.

[`Self::of`] prices usage as follows, given that the [`Usage`] counts
overlap: `cache_read` and a known `cache_write` are part of `input`, and
`reasoning` is part of `output`.

- Input tokens neither read from nor written to the cache bill at the input
  price.
- `cache_read` tokens bill at [`Pricing::cache_read_per_mtok_micro_usd`] and
  `cache_write` tokens at [`Pricing::cache_write_per_mtok_micro_usd`]; each
  falls back to the input price when the pricing declares no such price.
- Output tokens, reasoning included, bill at the output price.
- A usage whose `input` exceeds a declared long-context threshold bills at
  the long-context prices ([`Pricing::for_prompt`]), so price one request at
  a time.

The exact sum is rounded once to the nearest micro-USD, halves up, so a
run's cost, the sum of its requests' costs, can differ from pricing its
summed usage by less than one micro-USD per request. Arithmetic never
overflows: a cost beyond `u64::MAX` micro-USD saturates at it. A sum of
costs priced from different sources is [`PricingSource::Mixed`].

A model without [`Pricing`], such as a host model nobody priced, an
OpenAI-compatible server, or a plan-billed `ChatGPT` model whose marginal
requests are not metered, has no cost: `Option<Cost>` is `None` there.
On the wire it is `{"micro_usd": 1250, "pricing": "built_in"}`.

PricingSource.description:
Where a [`Pricing`] came from.

On the wire it is `built_in`, `host`, or `mixed`.

oneOf.description:
The harness's built-in list prices, as the providers published them
at their lowest input tier: Anthropic on 2026-11-21, the others on
2026-11-23. Claude Haiku 5.5 also carries its long-prompt prices.
Prices the host supplied, such as a negotiated rate.

Prices from more than one source, only on a summed
[`crate::Cost`], such as a session total over turns of differently
priced models; no [`Pricing`] has it.

Usage.description:
Provider-reported tokens, summed over a run's model requests.

The counts overlap: `cache_read` and a known `cache_write` are part of
`input`, and `reasoning` is part of `output`; [`crate::Cost`] prices them
accordingly. A count a provider omitted adds zero; a request whose
provider reported no input or output count is counted in
`unreported_requests`, so totals with unreported requests are lower
bounds. Requests the provider rejected as exceeding its context window,
and a request in flight when the run was cancelled, are not counted.

cache_read.description: Input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache.

cache_write.description:
Input tokens written to the provider's prompt cache, part of `input`,
or `None` when unknown; of the built-in protocols Anthropic Messages
reports them, and the `OpenAI` Responses API does for models from
GPT-5.6 on.

unreported_requests.description: Model requests whose provider reported no input or output count.

ContextActivity.description:
Content-free counts of how one provider request was reduced to fit the
context budget.

Reduction applies only to the copy sent to the provider: canonical turn
messages, durable journals, and replayed history keep the original
content. Counts describe the whole sent request, so a reduction carried
over from an earlier request of the same turn is counted again. All counts
are zero when the request was sent unchanged.

CompactionOutcome.description: How an automatic compaction attempt ended.

oneOf.description: A new checkpoint was published.

covered_through.description: Newest turn the published checkpoint covers.

model.description:
Catalog identifier of the model that answered the compaction
requests, as their [`RunEventKind::ModelRequestCompleted`]
events name it; `None` for a model the host supplied directly.
The checkpoint itself records the provider's model metadata.

oneOf.description:
The store held no uncovered turn to compact, for example because
another handle of the session published a checkpoint covering them
first. No model request was sent and the turn replays the store's
checkpoint.

Compaction failed, so the previous checkpoint stays and the turn
fell back to eviction.

ErrorKind.description:
Stable reason that a run or harness operation failed, for embedder retry
and recovery policy, by its wire name.

Every harness failure maps to exactly one kind. New kinds may be added as
the harness gains failure modes. Data a kind carries travels beside it.

oneOf.description: The caller cancelled the run.

The run reached one of its run limits or a budget ledger cap, named
beside the kind; retrying the same run would reach the same limit.

The provider limited the request rate; retry after
[`RunError::retry_after`] when present.

The provider was temporarily unavailable (HTTP `500`, `502`, `503`,
`504`, or `529`).
The provider rejected the credentials (HTTP `401` or `403`).
The provider account's quota or credit balance is spent.

The request exceeds the model's context window or budget, even after
every allowed reduction.

The model or provider returned output that is unusable: invalid JSON,
a schema violation, a malformed tool call, an undecodable response
envelope, or an oversized or incomplete response.
The network failed or the provider timed out the request.

A model request failed for a reason without a finer classification,
such as another provider rejection or a failure a custom
[`crate::Model`] reports through [`ModelError::request`].
A repository or sandbox tool failed in a way that ends the turn.
The model kept repeating tool calls without progress after a nudge.

The approval handler did not decide on a tool call within the
harness's approval timeout, so the call did not run.

The session already has an active turn or matching host request, or
the session store is temporarily locked or saturated.

The request conflicts with the session's recorded state, such as an
existing identifier, a reused host turn ID, or a stale handle.
The requested session does not exist.

The session store failed or holds invalid data, so the session's
durable state may be incomplete.

The harness, session, sandbox, or request configuration cannot be
satisfied, including capabilities the model does not support.

The run offers native-sandboxed `bash`, the sandbox cannot run on
this host, and the harness was told to refuse rather than run
commands without it; the error names what is missing.

LimitKind.description:
Which limit stopped a run: one of its [`RunLimits`], or a cap of the
budget ledger that refused its next model request.

It serializes as its `snake_case` name.

oneOf.description: [`RunLimits::max_model_requests`]: model requests.
[`RunLimits::max_tool_calls`]: tool calls.

[`RunLimits::max_total_tokens`] or a ledger's token cap: input plus
output tokens.
[`RunLimits::max_wall_time`]: wall-clock time.
A ledger's cost cap: micro-USD.

RunFailure.description:
A run's failure as plain data.

On the wire its `kind` is the [`ErrorKind::as_str`] name, and a
[`ErrorKind::BudgetExhausted`] failure adds the reached `limit`.

kind.description: Failure classification; `cancelled` for a cancelled run.

limit.description: The run limit a `budget_exhausted` failure reached.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the run may succeed.

SandboxUnavailableReason.description: What the native sandbox is missing on this host.

oneOf.description: The operating system has no native sandbox; only Linux and macOS do.

No helper executable: the configuration names none and the host did
not call [`dispatch`].

The helper is missing, not executable, set-ID, or inside the
workspace.

Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) is not installed at its configured path,
`/usr/bin/bwrap` by default.
Bubblewrap cannot create unprivileged user namespaces.

The configuration grants writes and the kernel cannot confine them
with Landlock, which needs Linux 6.2 or later.
`/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`, the macOS Seatbelt front end, is missing.

Seatbelt cannot start a sandbox, for example because this process
already runs inside one.

The configuration grants Unix-domain sockets, which only the macOS
sandbox can allow by path. Unlike the other reasons, commands still
run inside the sandbox, with every Unix-domain socket denied.

SandboxWarning.description:
Warning that a run's Bash commands execute without the native sandbox,
or, for [`SandboxUnavailableReason::UnixSocketsUnsupported`], inside it
without a grant it cannot honor, with what is missing and how to fix it.

message.description: What is missing, as [`SandboxUnavailableReason::message`] states it.

remedy.description: How to fix it, as [`SandboxUnavailableReason::remedy`] states it.

RunSummary.description: How a run finished, carried by [`RunEventKind::Completed`].

error.description: Why the run failed, or `None` when it produced its output.

usage.description: Tokens of every model request, as in [`crate::RunOutcome::usage`].
